niche: a regional air district's 2026 NOx inventory of the boilers and process heaters its NOx rule covers, conformed from continuous monitors, two source test databases, the facilities' fuel statements and the gas utility's monthly heat content by BTU area, to name the five facilities its 2027 community plan's NOx agreements cover
answer: Sign the 2027 NOx reduction agreements with Ashgrove Refining, Lindqvist Paperboard, Merriwell Foods, Sedge Hollow Creamery and Valmora Glass Works, against Tamsett State University in sixth (provisional at the draw; the tons come from generator/figures.json at stage 3).
answer_source: design note at the draw; submission.md block 1 from generator/figures.json once built
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms every source test to lb/MMBtu, every fuel statement to heat input (MMscf at the utility's heat content for the facility's BTU area and month) and every monitor hour to 2026, and reads the plan and its guidance correctly, carries each unmonitored burner's latest test (or the mean of its tests, or the monitored boiler's 2026 months as an index) across its 2026 fuel and names Ashgrove Refining, Lindqvist Paperboard, Sedge Hollow Creamery, Tamsett State University and Valmora Glass Works; only each burner's tests carried from the heating value of their months' gas to each 2026 month's, by the rise of NOx with heating value that the monitored Lindqvist power boiler traces against the utility's monthly heat content, names Ashgrove Refining, Lindqvist Paperboard, Merriwell Foods, Sedge Hollow Creamery and Valmora Glass Works.
domain_test: Stationary-source inventory work: a source test is a snapshot of a unit's NOx rate on its test day's fuel, and a low-NOx burner that meters its combustion air by volume burns a richer gas hotter, so its NOx rises several per cent for each per cent the supply's heating value rises; the year's NOx needs each test carried across the heating values the year's gas ran at; with hospital or traffic nouns there is no burner air-fuel ratio, no gas heating value and no source test to carry, so nothing is left to decide.
layer2_pattern: own:a spot test of an emission rate read on its day's fuel, carried across the year month by month by the fuel's heating value, the sensitivity read from a monitored unit of the same burner type and the units' own test histories against the supplier's monthly record
layer1: source tests split across two databases, ppmvd at 3 per cent oxygen and lb/hr in the older, lb/MMBtu added in the newer
fuel statements in therms, MMscf and MMBtu by facility layout, MMscf converted at the utility's heat content for the facility's BTU area and month
monitor hours in local standard time with substitute-data codes
district device numbers against the monitoring plan's unit ids and the test databases' keys without leading zeros
an event log with mixed date formats and free text, the notices and retests a failed test brings
a facility renumbered after a change of owner
a test deferred past its due date under a filed extension

spine.entity: one hour of one continuously monitored unit
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a continuous emissions monitoring hourly export)

invented_names: Tamsett Basin Air Pollution Control District

driver: The decisive quantity is each unit's period total of an output whose rate rises steeply with a property of an input a third party supplies, which the supplier records month by month for each supply area and which moves without any event at the unit; most units are measured only by occasional spot tests, each read on whatever input its day received, so carrying a spot test across the period, or averaging a unit's tests, misstates every unit whose period ran on a different input from its test days, while a continuously measured unit of the same kind and the units' own test histories trace the rate against the supplier's record, which carries each test from its test month's input to each month's.
driver_concrete: Each facility's 2026 NOx from its Rule 4306 boilers and heaters is mostly its unmonitored low-NOx burners' fuel times a rate that rises about six per cent for each per cent the Westside BTU area's gas heating value rises, because a burner metering its air by volume burns a richer gas hotter; a source test reads the rate on its test day's gas, so Merriwell Foods' boilers, tested in the lean Augusts of odd years, understate a 2026 season that ran on rich gas, and Tamsett State University's, tested in rich Mays, overstate a winter fired on lean gas, while the monitored Lindqvist power boiler traces the rise against the utility's monthly heat content.
stump: The default path carries each unmonitored burner's latest source test across its 2026 fuel and names Ashgrove Refining, Lindqvist Paperboard, Sedge Hollow Creamery, Tamsett State University and Valmora Glass Works; a low-NOx burner that meters its combustion air by volume burns a richer gas hotter, so its NOx rises with the heating value of the gas its BTU area receives, which the Westside gas plant's ethane recovery moves from month to month: Merriwell Foods' boilers were last tested in August 2025 on lean gas and ran their 2026 season on rich gas, and Tamsett State University's were tested in May 2026 on rich gas and fired the winter on lean; the rise the monitored Lindqvist power boiler traces against the utility's monthly heat content, carried from each test's month to each 2026 month, names Ashgrove Refining, Lindqvist Paperboard, Merriwell Foods, Sedge Hollow Creamery and Valmora Glass Works.

differentiation.task478: architecture 6 carried each test along the operating hours on its catalyst, a clock the unit's own maintenance log builds; here no part ages and nothing at the unit changes: the rate follows a property of the fuel a third party supplies, recorded only in that supplier's monthly table
differentiation.task190: task190 judges a ratio's departure against its sampling error, the numerator complete and the denominator a stratified estimate; here no interval decides anything: each spot test is carried across the year by the heating value of the gas a third party delivered each month
differentiation.task195: task195 judges a paired difference between two screens by its own uncertainty; here nothing is tested against noise: each unit's spot test is carried to the year by the rise of its rate with the fuel's heating value
differentiation.task228: task228 identifies each instrument's random error from the covariances of independent measurements of one signal; here no error is separated: the measured rate itself follows a property of the delivered fuel, and the year needs it carried month by month

lineage.driver: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles in March 2027 counts the potholes no camera unit recorded, completed segment by segment as one over the chance that at least one of the distinct installed units that drove the segment found a pothole, the per-unit chance (0.542) read from how often a second unit found a pothole another unit found; a unit records the same potholes on every pass (99.5 per cent of its later days), so a segment its section's patrol pickup drove on seven or more days has had one chance.
lineage.stump: The default path completes the potholes no unit recorded by treating every pass over a segment as an independent chance at the rate a pass re-finds a found pothole (64 per cent of unit-days), which changes nothing on segments driven seven or more times, and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt only; the rural and outer suburban sections one unit drove hide close to half their potholes, and Fenwick Gap, Thistlebank, Holloway Run, Kestrelton and Norvelle clear the line at 7.08 to 8.29.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: reader G (the ninth isolated reader) landed the call by distinct-unit capture-recapture; readers C to H kept ask A's counts and two kept the camera miles

lineage.driver: Distinct entities are counted from repeated positional reports by instruments of unequal accuracy, each instrument's error measured on surveyed control objects, so reports are linked within a tolerance that follows the instrument; any single tolerance either splits a noisy instrument's reports of one entity or merges an accurate instrument's reports of distinct neighbours.
lineage.stump: The default path links the pothole detections into potholes with one milepost tolerance for every unit and designates another set at any tolerance it picks; the street sweepers' older Kerbline units place their reports of one pothole tens of feet apart while the patrol units' reports of neighbouring bridge-deck potholes sit a few yards apart, so only a tolerance set by each unit's error on the surveyed utility covers resolves both.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: readers C and D landed the call by folding the sweepers' visibly scattered reports into the precise units' potholes; the camera miles ask leaked to both round 1 readers and was dropped

lineage.driver: A count seen through several instruments is completed by multiple-list recapture, and instruments of one family see the same members while different families see independently, so the occasions are the distinct families that looked at a unit at the cross-family recapture rate, not the instruments; taking every instrument as independent overstates the find rate and completes too little.
lineage.stump: The default path completes pass by pass and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt; the careful path takes every installed unit as an independent chance at 69.9 per cent and designates five; units of one fleet group record 93.6 per cent of each other's potholes against 54.9 per cent across groups, so the chances are the fleet groups at 54.4 per cent, and Fenwick Gap (6.86) and Kestrelton (7.28) join Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: round 2 reader D landed the call and all 14 rates by estimating each fleet group's visibility by maximum likelihood after seeing units of one group agree 93 to 100 per cent; the judge noted a unit-level truncated MLE also landed the seven

lineage.driver: Distinct entities are counted from position reports that each instrument displaces along its direction of travel by its own latency times its speed, so one entity seen in both directions appears as two tight clusters; the latency is calibrated on control objects of surveyed position and each report corrected by its pass's direction and speed before linking, while any single linking distance either splits the two directions or merges close neighbours.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles counts the distinct potholes its Kerbline detections resolve to after each detection is moved back along its pass by its unit's GPS latency (measured against the asset inventory's surveyed utility covers) times the pass's speed from the telematics traversals, because every phone places what it sees ahead of where it is, northbound to the north and southbound to the south.
lineage.stump: The default path links the pothole detections at one distance and designates Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle at anything from 132 to 410 feet, or a seven with Grisholt and Oxbrae at 54 to 124 feet, because every Kerbline phone places a detection ahead of the pothole along its direction of travel by its own GPS latency times its speed, so on the two-lane roads one pothole seen both ways is two clusters while the bridge decks' neighbouring potholes sit closer than that; each detection moved back by its unit's latency on the surveyed covers at its own pass's speed and direction, the detections designate the seven.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-22 at stage 4: reader F of eight landed the call by fitting each unit's lag from cluster offsets on the pass's signed speed; a displacement proportional to speed is identifiable from the clusters themselves, so the surveyed covers were a convenience

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the share of a measured population above a fixed limit, read through instruments that each carry their own multiplicative bias; a component of every unit whose true size depends only on a coarse state and not on the quantity the limit tests is read by the same instruments, so its level at each instrument, matched by that state to a reference reading of the same component, measures the instrument's bias, and dividing each reading by it before counting moves the ranking the raw readings give, while matching unlike states moves it again.
lineage.stump: The default path counts each section's class 9 trucks over 80,000 lb on the gross its weigh-in-motion station recorded and equips Brannock, Cole Hollow, Garnet Ridge, Ingram Mill and Jessup Fork; each station reads every axle through its own calibration (Brannock's, Foxbriar's and Ingram Mill's 5 to 7 per cent heavy, Elk Ferry's and Kettle Run's 4 to 5 per cent light), which only its loaded tractors' steer-axle median against the scale houses' loaded static tickets measures, because a loaded tractor's steer axle does not move with the cargo while the tickets are pulled-in heavy trucks and the sections haul different freight.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-22: reader C (round 2) landed the call by measuring each station's gain on the vehicle classes other than 9 against the four stations that agree, and kept all 24 ask figures

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is each unit's period total of an output whose rate climbs with the operating hours since a component was last renewed; most units are measured only by occasional spot tests, each taken at whatever renewal age its day fell on, so carrying a spot test across the period as a constant misstates the period, while the climb the units' own test histories trace against their hours since renewal, integrated over the hours the period ran through, does not.
lineage.stump: The default path carries each unmonitored unit's latest source test across its 2026 fuel and names Ashgrove Refining, Haskett Ridge, Lindqvist Paperboard, Valmora Glass and Wexley Point; a unit injecting ammonia open-loop emits NOx at a rate that climbs with the operating hours on its catalyst since the last replacement, so Sedge Hollow's and St. Aldric's tests, read weeks after new catalysts went in, understate engines that ran on them all 2026 and Haskett Ridge's, read on catalysts replaced that December, overstate it, and the climb the test histories trace against catalyst hours names Ashgrove Refining, Sedge Hollow, St. Aldric Medical Center, Valmora Glass and Wexley Point.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-23: reader A (round 1) landed the call by fitting each unit's tests on the operating hours since its last catalyst event (one shared climb, a level per unit); reader B missed it
